**Slides.** [Open the deck at this part](../../slides/eu-frames-one-day-methods.html#/part-1-the-case-and-the-vocabulary){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).

Part 1 sets out the case and the vocabulary: why social science is argued about at all, the matrix that separates reproducing from replicating, and the five analysts who reanalysed the claim that the day works on. It ends with R running on every machine.

| Work through | What you do | Timing |
|---|---|---|
| Slides, the opening | The plan of the day, the two kinds of aim, and what you do not need. Open the browser lab in a tab and leave it to load. | 6 minutes |
| Slides, the credibility talk | What social science is for, false positives and forking paths, incentives, and the twenty-nine teams of the red-card study, grouped by the response distribution that each team assumed, a grouping to keep in mind for the rest of the day. | 20 minutes |
| Slides, the vocabulary | Why 'replication' names three operations; the matrix of data and analysis; repeatability and credibility; the quick check on the matrix in peer review; the practices of open research. | 15 minutes |
| Slides, Multi100 from the inside | What a Multi100 analyst received, the paper in brief, the two Multi100 tasks, how their results are put on a common scale, and a forest plot of the five analysts' results, one row at a time. | 22 minutes |
| Slides on the browser lab, then [Browser lab](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd) Task 1 | Get to the point where a line of R runs and the panel of 270 country-years is in front of you. | 27 minutes with the slides, and the 30-minute break after it if you need more |

**By the end of the part** R runs on your machine, you can tell apart the three operations that go under the word 'replication', and you have the results of the five analysts in front of you as the puzzle that the rest of the day works on.
